items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5965

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the civil service law, in relation to compensation,
benefits and other terms and conditions of employment of certain
members of the security supervisors unit who are employed by the state
department of correctional services and are designated as peace
officers; to amend the state finance law, in relation to the employee
benefit fund for certain members of the security supervisors unit; to
provide for the payment of a firearms training and safety incentive
for peace officers who are members of the professional, scientific and
professional services bargaining unit; to implement an interest
arbitration award issued between the state and the employee
organization representing certain members of the security supervisors
unit; to make an appropriation for the purpose of effectuating certain
of the provisions thereof; and to repeal certain provisions of the
civil service law relating thereto


 PURPOSE :

This bill would implement the provisions of an interest arbitration
award ("Award") issued pursuant to Civil Service Law ("CSL") § 209(4)
binding the executive branch of New York State and the employee
organization ("Council 82") representing members of the Security
Supervisors collective negotiating unit who are employed by the State
Department of Correctional Services and are designated as peace
officers pursuant to Criminal Procedure Law ("CPL") § 2.10(25)
("members of the unit" or "unit members").

This bill would also provide for the payment of a Firearms Training
and Safety Incentive to peace officers who are members of the
Professional, Scientific and Technical Services Unit pursuant to the
terms of a pilot program collectively negotiated by New York State and
the employee organization representing such members, pursuant to
Article 14 of the CSL, to rectify an omission in a previous bill.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 of this bill would repeal CSL § 130(1)(j)(1) and (2) and add
new subparagraphs 1, 2 and 3 to CSL § 130(1)(j) to establish salary
schedules covering members of the unit to reflect increases in basic
annual salary, effective April 1, 2005, April 1, 2006 and March 31,
2007 as set forth in § 3 of this bill.

Section 2 of this bill would amend State Finance Law ("SFL") §
207-a(2-a) to provide for the continuation of employer payments to the
employee benefit fund established by Council 82 for members of the
unit. Such payments will reflect an increase in the contribution per
unit member, effective April 1, 2006, from $25 to $30 for those unit
members who were on the payroll on the last day of the payroll period
in which March 1, 2006 fell.

Section 3 of this bill would provide for the compensation of
applicable members of the unit in accordance with the terms of the
Award, including:

* a 2.25% salary increase, effective April 1, 2005; a 2.75% salary
increase, effective April 1, 2006; and a $3,050 salary increase,
effective March 31, 2007 to reflect the addition of the uniform
maintenance allowance and security enforcement differential to basic
annual salary;
* advancement payments to members of the unit pursuant to CSL § 131
(6); and
* enhanced longevity step payments.
This section would also give to the Director of the Budget and the
Director of Employee Relations discretion to withhold all or a portion
of a unit member's salary increase, where any such increase would not
be appropriate or warranted.

Section 4 of this bill would provide additional compensation to
members of the unit, in accordance with the terms of the Award, in
recognition of the general requirement for full-time employees to
assemble for briefing prior to the commencement of their duties.

Section 5 of this bill would continue the payment of an annual
corrections clothing maintenance allowance of $1,500 to members of the
unit. Effective March 31, 2007, however, such allowance would be
included in basic annual salary of members of the unit and no longer
identified as a separate benefit.

Section 6 of this bill would provide location pay for members of the
unit whose official work station is located in New York City and the
counties of Nassau, Suffolk, Westchester, Rockland, Orange, Putnam and
Dutchess, pursuant to the terms of the Award, as follows:

* Effective April 1, 2005:

Orange, Putnam, Dutchess        $1,092
NYC, Rockland, Westchester      $2,938
Nassau, Suffolk                 $3,092

* Effective April 1, 2006:

Orange, Putnam, Dutchess        $1,126
NYC, Rockland, Westchester      $3,026
Nassau, Suffolk                 $3,093


The  location  payment  will  be  equally  divided over the 26 payroll
periods in each  fiscal  year  and  will  count  as  compensation  for
overtime and retirement purposes.

Section 7 of this bill would provide for the payment to members of the
unit  of  a  security  enforcement differential in the amount of $850,
effective  April  1,  2005,  and  $1,100,  effective  April  1,  2006.
Effective  March  31,  2007, such differential in the amount of $1,550
would be included in the basic annual salary of such  members  and  no
longer identified as separate benefit.

Section 8 of this bill would provide for an inconvenience pay program,
effective  April  1,  2006, which would pay $900 or $1,800 annually to
those unit  members  who  work  the  night  shift  or  evening  shift,
respectively.

Section  9 of this bill would continue the annual payment of $1,500 to
members of the  unit  in  recognition  of  their  command  duties  and
responsibilities  performed  with regard to infectious disease, mental
health, crime scene control, prisoner transport and other inter-agency
issues which arise in correctional facilities.

Section 10 of this bill would provide for the continuation of a  joint
committee  on health benefits to be funded in the amount of $6,400 for
the period April 1, 2005 to March 31, 2006, and $6,400 for the  period
April  1,  2006  to  March 31, 2007. One-half of these amounts will be
made available to both the State and Council 82.

Section 11 of this bill would provide for the payment  of  a  Firearms
Training and Safety Incentive to peace officers who are members of the
Professional,  Scientific and Technical Services Unit, pursuant to the

terms of a pilot program collectively negotiated between the  employee
organization representing such members and New York State.

Section 12 of this bill would make the appropriations contained in the
bill   available   for   the  payment  and  publication  of  grievance
arbitration settlements and awards.

Section 13 of this bill would provide that no increase in compensation
set forth in the bill would be payable  to  an  individual  until  and
unless he or she is a member of unit, employed by the State Department
of Correctional Services and designated as a peace officer pursuant to
CPL § 2.10(25).

Section  14 of the bill would continue to exempt the salaries of newly
hired unit members from the ,imposition of "deferred payment" pursuant
to SFL § 200(2-a).

Section 15 of the bill would set the date upon which incumbent members
of the unit would receive the salary increases provided by the Award.

Section 16 of the bill  would  provide  that  until  payment  is  made
pursuant  to  this  bill,  members  of  the  unit will receive payment
otherwise payable in their respective positions.   When  basic  annual
salaries  are  first paid pursuant to this bill, such members shall be
entitled to a lump sum payment for the difference between the salaries
to which they were entitled since April 1, 2005 and  the  compensation
actually received.

Section  17  of  the  bill  would authorize the Comptroller to pay any
amounts  required  by  the  bill.  To   the   extent   that   existing
appropriations  available  to  any  State  department  or  agency  are
insufficient to accomplish the purposes set forth in this section, the
Director of the Budget would be authorized to allocate to the  various
departments and agencies the amounts necessary to make such payments.

Section  18  of the bill would appropriate approximately $17.2 million
in the General Fund to pay for personal and non-personal services  for
members  of  the  unit as provided in this bill and in accordance with
the terms of the Award.

Section 19 of the bill would provide that it take  effect  immediately
and be deemed to have been in full force and effect on and after April
1,  2005,  except  for § 11 of the bill, which would be deemed to have
been in full force and effect on and after April 1, 2008.

 EXISTING LAW :

Chapter 4 of the Laws of 2007 sets forth several terms and  conditions
of  employment  relating  to compensation for members of the unit from
April 1, 2003 to March 31, 2005. In addition, Chapter 375 of the  Laws
of  2007  sets  forth  several  terms  of conditions of employment not
directly relating to compensation for the time period beginning  April
1, 2003 and ending March 31, 2007.

CSL  § 130(1)(j) sets forth the current salary and longevity schedules
for members of the unit.

CSL § 134(5) provides for the current pre-shift briefing payment.

Chapter 114 of the  Laws  of  2008  implements  the  provisions  of  a
collective  bargaining  agreement  between the Executive Branch of the
State of New  York  and  the  employee  organization  that  represents
members  of  the Professional, Scientific and Technical Services Unit,
for period beginning April 2, 2007 and ending April 1, 2011.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
None.

 STATEMENT IN SUPPORT :

This  bill  is  necessary  to  implement  the  terms  of  an  interest
arbitration award issued pursuant to CSL § 209(4), binding  the  State
of  New York and the employee organization representing members of the
Security Supervisors collective negotiating unit.

Section 11 of this bill is necessary to implement  a  provision  of  a
collective  bargaining agreement between the State of New York and the
employee organization that represents  members  of  the  Professional,
Scientific  and  Technical  Services  Unit,  which  was  inadvertently
omitted from a previous bill.

 BUDGET IMPLICATIONS :

This bill would  provide  for  appropriations  totaling  approximately
$17.27  million,  all  of which is within the General Fund, to pay for
the cost of the interest arbitration award covering the  period  April
1, 2005 to March 31, 2007. The 2009-10 financial plan accommodates the
costs associated with this bill.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This  bill would take effect immediately and be deemed to have been in
full force and effect on and after April 1, 2005, except for §  11  of
the  bill, which would be deemed to have been in full force and effect
on and after April 1, 2008.

summary: Relates to compensation, benefits and other terms and conditions of employment of certain members of the security supervisors unit who are employed by the state department of correctional services and are designated as peace officers, to the employee benefit fund for certain members of the security supervisors unit; provides for the payment of a firearms training and safety incentive for peace officers who are members of the professional, scientific and professional services bargaining unit; implements an interest arbitration award issued between the state and the employee organization representing certain members of the security supervisors unit; makes an appropriation for the purpose of effectuating certain provisions thereof; repeals certain provisions of the civil service law relating thereto.
